title: Broadening the reflection band of atomic mirrors by engineering the emitter-waveguide coupling
authors: C. -Y. Lee, G. -D. Lin, H. H. Jen, K. -T. Lin
abstract: We theoretically investigate single-photon coherent transport through a finite waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) array with spatially modulated emitter-waveguide couplings. By combining exact scattering calculations with spectral factorization and a semiclassical WKB analysis, we identify how the coupling profile controls the reflection bandwidth and its finite-size dependence. A Gaussian transverse displacement produces an exponential-of-Gaussian decay-rate profile that broadens the high-reflectivity window and suppresses the boundary-induced Fabry-Perot oscillations compared with a uniform array. The transmission zeros remain exactly degenerate at the atomic resonance for arbitrary positive coupling profiles at non-Bragg spacings. In contrast, the collective poles reorganize under the spatial modulation, redistributing their radiative widths and preventing individual subradiant resonances from terminating the reflection window. We further derive an algebraic 1/N scaling law for the contraction of the bandwidth toward its bulk value. The bulk bandwidth is determined by the largest local decay rate, whereas the finite-size correction increases as the profile becomes sharper, leading to an optimal profile width. These results establish spatial coupling engineering as a practical tool for designing broadband atomic mirrors in atom-nanofiber and circuit-QED platforms.
summary: This theoretical study demonstrates that by spatially engineering the coupling strength between emitters and a waveguide, one can significantly broaden the reflection band of atomic mirrors. Using advanced scattering and WKB methods, the authors show that this engineering equalizes the radiative widths of collective modes, leading to broadband, high-reflectivity windows. This establishes coupling profile design as a powerful tool for quantum optical device realization.
main_problem: The paper investigates how engineering the coupling between emitters and a waveguide can broaden the reflection band of atomic mirrors.
main_result: A Gaussian coupling profile successfully broadens the high-reflectivity window and suppresses detrimental Fabry-Perot oscillations compared to uniform arrays. Furthermore, an algebraic 1/N scaling law for the bandwidth contraction toward the bulk limit was derived.
method: The study employs exact scattering calculations combined with spectral factorization and a semiclassical WKB analysis on the single-excitation sector.
model_or_system: The system is a finite array of $N$ two-level emitters coupled to a 1D waveguide in a Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) setup. The dynamics are governed by an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Reflection bandwidth, transmission ($t$) and reflection ($r$) amplitudes, and the distribution of collective poles in the complex frequency plane.
important_parameters: The coupling profile width ($\sigma$), the number of emitters ($N$), and the local decay rates ($\gamma_j$) are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis operates within the single-excitation sector, the Markovian approximation, and assumes linear photon dispersion.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the reflection spectrum $|r|^2$ vs. detuning ($\Delta$) for different coupling strengths, showing broadening, and map the high-reflectivity bandwidth across the coupling parameter space.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical model and Hamiltonian, to applying scattering theory to analyze the reflection spectrum, and finally deriving the finite-size scaling laws by mapping the problem to a continuous Helmholtz equation.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, tunable methods (spatial coupling engineering) to overcome fundamental limitations (Fabry-Perot oscillations) in designing high-performance quantum optical components like atomic mirrors.

N two-level emitters are coupled to a bidirectional 1D waveguide with uniform interatomic spacing d along the propagation axis (z axis). The local spontaneous decay rates γ j are modulated by tailored transverse displacements of the emitters relative to the waveguide axis. Because the guided mode is evanescent in the transverse direction, such displacements modify the local coupling strength exponentially.
